name: Genetic Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Corneal Dystrophies

criteria.description: Positive family history of corneal dystrophy consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Presence of characteristic bilateral corneal opacities or deposits on slit-lamp examination
Identification of pathogenic variants in known corneal dystrophy-associated genes (e.g., TGFBI, CHST6)
Corneal biopsy showing typical dystrophic deposits or abnormal extracellular matrix

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic bilateral corneal opacities with either a positive family history or pathogenic genetic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and subtype classification.

pathognomonic.notes: Painful episodes often triggered by minor trauma

common.notes: Progressive vision impairment due to corneal clouding
Light sensitivity associated with corneal surface irregularities

common.symptomName: Foreign body sensation in the eye

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to chronic epithelial defects
Resulting from recurrent erosions or ulcerations
Associated with episodes of erosion or inflammation

rare.notes: Rare complication due to corneal pathology
Uncommon corneal ectasia in some dystrophy subtypes

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in TGFBI, CHST6, or other corneal dystrophy-associated genes
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing characteristic corneal deposits and opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing corneal layer involvement
genetic: Autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance patterns depending on subtype
Pathogenic variants in genes such as TGFBI, CHST6, UBIAD1
other: Histopathological examination of corneal tissue showing amyloid, granular, or lattice deposits depending on dystrophy subtype

distinguishingFeatures: No family history in many cases
Superficial epithelial basement membrane abnormalities without stromal deposits
Usually no family history of corneal dystrophy

redFlags: Recurrent severe corneal erosions with pain and photophobia
Development of corneal ulceration or secondary infection
references: Krachmer JH, Mannis MJ, Holland EJ. Cornea: Fundamentals, Diagnosis and Management. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2011.
Weiss JS, Møller HU, Lisch W, et al. IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies--edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
